goal: `mc publish` is the one way a step's session or a mend puts a new head on its pull request: it edits only the fields it is given, can retarget the base, publishes a detached HEAD to a named branch, and keeps the description honest by listing the commits that came after it.
Nothing mc tells a session sends it past `mc publish`: the retry preamble, the mend prompt, the pre-tool hook, the toolbox and the help all name it.
`mc merge` refuses an unpushed head or a conflicting pull request at the door, and the merger lands only the head it measured.
contract: `mc publish` never force-pushes and never opens a second pull request for a branch; its existing refusals (main, a dirty tree, a remote branch that moved) stay as they are.
The text of a description above `## After the description` is never changed by `mc publish` unless `--body` or `--body-file` is given.
`remainderOf` still returns exactly what it returns today for a body without `<!-- mc:` lines.
The merger's gate, its selection and its verdicts are unchanged; only the landing call and the door before the queue change.
out_of_scope: `mc gate` and the test rounds (`mc test`, `runGate`, the nightly) — planned separately after the test review Martin asked for on 2026-10-16.
memoro's `AGENTS.md` *Deterministic publication sequence* and § *Landing a stack* — rewritten in memoro once this project has landed.
The false 'NOT the measured build' warning, `MC_STEP` attribution (proposal `2026-10-12-merge-attributes-foreign-pr-to-blocked-step.md`) and the `project_log.md` duplicate check.
Stripping `<!-- mc:` lines from the squash commit message GitHub builds.

No prompt, hook reason, toolbox line or help text mc gives a session tells it to run `git push` or `gh pr edit`.

steps.title: `mc publish` edits only the fields it is given, and takes `--base`
steps.done_when: `node --test --import ./tests/_isolate-home.mjs tests/mc/publish.test.js` passes with the three new tests, and `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why (ruling 43): today, on a branch with an open pull request, `mc publish --body-file f` runs `gh pr edit N --title <last commit subject> --body <f>`, so a fix commit's subject replaces the title; `--title` alone likewise replaces the body with the last commit's. Sessions went to `gh pr edit` by hand instead.

In `src/mc/commands/publish.js`: add `'--base'` to `strictValues` in the `scanArgs` call (it becomes `flags.base`, as `--body-file` becomes `flags.bodyFile`). In the `if (open)` branch, build the edit arguments from what was given: start with `['pr', 'edit', String(open.number)]`, push `'--title', flags.title` only when `flags.title` is set, `'--body', bodyGiven` only when `bodyGiven != null`, `'--base', flags.base` only when `flags.base` is set; run `gh` only when at least one was pushed. In the `else` branch (create), the base is `flags.base || defaultBase(git)`. Nothing else in the flow changes.

Update the file's top comment (the `gh pr edit` sentence: 'or `gh pr edit` of exactly the fields given — title, body, base — when the branch already has an open pull request') and `usage()`: add the line `'        mc publish --base <branch>          the base a new pull request aims at, or the open one is moved to\n'` after the `--body-file` line, and change the `--title` line's tail to `named instead; on an open pull request each edits only its own field`.

In `src/mc/help-text.js`, the `mc publish [--title …] [--body …]` entry: make the usage `mc publish [--title …] [--body-file …] [--base …]` and change 'title and body from the last commit unless given' to 'title and body from the last commit for a new one; on an open one, edits only the fields given'. Keep the column layout of the neighbouring entries. In `docs/mc-command-matrix.md`, the `mc publish` row: add `[--base <b>]` to the usage cell and replace '— or `gh pr edit` when the branch already has an open pull request and a title or body was given, never a second one —' with '— or, when the branch already has an open pull request, `gh pr edit` of exactly the fields given (`--title`, `--body`/`--body-file`, `--base`), never a second one —'.

Tests in `tests/mc/publish.test.js`, inside `describe('mc publish')`, using the existing `fixture` with `remote: 'bbbbbbb\trefs/heads/step-x', prs: [{ number: 4, url: 'https://x/pull/4' }]`: (1) `'on an open pull request --body edits the body alone'` — `run(['--body', 'B'])` gives `gh[1]` deep-equal `['pr', 'edit', '4', '--body', 'B']`; (2) `'--title edits the title alone, --base the base alone'` — `['--title', 'T']` gives `['pr', 'edit', '4', '--title', 'T']`, and a fresh fixture with `['--base', 'release']` gives `['pr', 'edit', '4', '--base', 'release']`; (3) `'a new pull request aims at --base when given'` — default fixture, `['--base', 'release']`, `gh[1]` is `['pr', 'create', '--base', 'release', '--head', 'step-x', '--title', 'The subject', '--body', 'The body.']`. Keep the existing test at line ~90; its `['--title', 'New', '--body', 'B']` case still expects `['pr', 'edit', '4', '--title', 'New', '--body', 'B']`.

steps.title: The description carries the head it describes, and `mc publish` lists the commits after it
steps.done_when: `node --test --import ./tests/_isolate-home.mjs tests/mc/publish.test.js tests/mc/merge-command.test.js` passes with the new tests, and `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why (ruling 43): a fix pushed after review left the description describing the first head, and the merger books that description. The description now ends with `<!-- mc:described <sha> -->`, and every `mc publish` without a body lists, under a generated section, the commits after that sha.

Pure helpers in `src/mc/publish.js` (exported, each with a short doc comment in the file's style). `AFTER_HEADING = '## After the description'`. `markedBody(text, sha)` returns `text.trimEnd()` + `'

'` + `<!-- mc:described ${sha} -->` (just the mark when `text.trim()` is empty). `readBody(body)` returns `{ text, described }`: `described` is the 40- or 7-to-40-hex sha of the last line matching `/^<!-- mc:described ([0-9a-f]{7,40}) -->$/u` (null when none); `text` is the body with that line removed and, when a line equal to `AFTER_HEADING` exists, everything from that line on removed, then `trimEnd()`. `afterSection(commits)` takes `[{ sha, subject, body }]` oldest first and returns `''` for none, else `AFTER_HEADING + '

'` followed by one entry per commit: `- \`${sha.slice(0, 7)}\` ${subject}`, then each non-empty line of `body` indented two spaces, leaving out lines matching `/^(Co-Authored-By|Claude-Session|Signed-off-by):/iu`; entries separated by one newline. `describedBody({ text, described, commits })` returns `markedBody(afterSection(commits) ? `${text.trimEnd()}

${afterSection(commits)}` : text, described)`.

In `src/mc/commands/publish.js`: on create, the body passed to `gh pr create` is `markedBody(body, localHead)`. On an open pull request with `bodyGiven != null`, the `--body` value is `markedBody(bodyGiven, localHead)`. On an open pull request with no body given: read `gh(['pr', 'view', String(open.number), '--json', 'body'])` and `readBody` it. `described` is the mark's sha, or — when there is none — the first line of `git(['rev-list', '--reverse', '--no-merges', `origin/${flags.base || defaultBase(git)}..HEAD`])`. If `described` is null, or `git(['merge-base', '--is-ancestor', described, 'HEAD']) === null`, write `mc: the description's head ${described || '(none)'} is not in this branch — left as it is; write it again with --body-file\n` to stderr and edit nothing. Otherwise list the commits with `git(['log', '--reverse', '--no-merges', '--format=%H%x1f%s%x1f%b%x1e', `${described}..HEAD`])`, split on `\x1e` and `\x1f` (trim each record, skip empty ones), build `describedBody`, and only when it differs from the body as read add `'--body', <it>` to the edit arguments step 1 builds — one `gh pr edit` call, carrying `--title`/`--base` too when those were given, and none when nothing was added. Count the listed commits as `after` for the output.

Output: `publishLines` takes an optional `after` (number). When `after > 0`, add after the 'opened/already open' line: `description at ${described.slice(0, 7)}; ${after} later commit${after === 1 ? '' : 's'} under "After the description" — --body-file rewrites it`. `--json` carries `described` and `after`.
`remainderOf` in `src/mc/merge-step.js`: drop every line matching `/^<!-- mc:[^>]*-->$/u` from `lines` before searching (so the mark never ends up in a remainder); nothing else changes.

Tests. In `tests/mc/publish.test.js`, give the fixture a `body` option (default `''`) that a `['pr', 'view', N, '--json', 'body']` call returns as `{ body }`, and a `log` option answering `git log --reverse --no-merges --format=...` (default `''`) and `rev-list` (default `'aaaaaaa1111'`). Update the first test's expected create body to `'The body.

<!-- mc:described aaaaaaa1111 -->'`. New: (1) `'readBody and describedBody round-trip, and a second publish changes nothing'` — pure: `readBody(describedBody({ text: 'Intro', described: 'abc1234', commits: [{ sha: 'def5678aaaa', subject: 'Fix it', body: 'Why.

Co-Authored-By: x' }] }))` gives `{ text: 'Intro', described: 'abc1234' }`, and that body contains `- \`def5678\` Fix it
  Why.` and not `Co-Authored-By`; (2) `'an open pull request with later commits gets them under After the description, and only the body is edited'` — `body: 'Intro

<!-- mc:described ccccccc -->'`, `log` one record for sha `ddddddd0000` subject `Fix` body `''`; expect one `['pr', 'edit', '4', '--body', ...]` call whose body is `'Intro

## After the description

- `ddddddd` Fix

<!-- mc:described ccccccc -->'`, and stdout containing `1 later commit`; (3) `'nothing after the mark: no edit'` — same body, empty `log`; the gh calls are `list`, `view` (body), `view` (snapshot), no `edit`. In `tests/mc/merge-command.test.js` next to the `remainderOf` test: `remainderOf('## Remainder
One thing.

<!-- mc:described abc1234 -->')` is `'One thing.'`.

Docs: in `docs/mc-command-matrix.md`'s `mc publish` row add one sentence: 'The description ends with `<!-- mc:described <sha> -->`; without a body, the commits after that head are listed under a regenerated `## After the description` (ruling 43).'

steps.title: `mc publish --branch <name>` publishes a detached HEAD
steps.done_when: `node --test --import ./tests/_isolate-home.mjs tests/mc/publish.test.js` passes with the new tests, and `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why (ruling 43): a mend's worktree is `origin/<branch>`, detached (`src/mc/mend.js`, `worktree add --detach`), so `mc publish` refuses it as `HEAD`; the mend must still publish through it.

In `src/mc/commands/publish.js`: add `'--branch'` to `strictValues`. After reading `rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` into `current`: when `flags.branch` is set and `current !== 'HEAD' && current !== flags.branch`, write `mc: --branch ${flags.branch}, but this worktree is on ${current} — drop --branch\n` and return 2; when `git(['check-ref-format', '--branch', flags.branch]) === null`, write `mc: --branch ${flags.branch} is not a branch name\n` and return 2. `branch` is `flags.branch || current`. Everything after uses `branch` as today, so main/master refusals, the dirty-tree refusal and the moved-remote refusal apply unchanged.

`pushBranch(cwd, branch, { spawn, stderr, detached = false })`: when `detached`, the push arguments are `['push', ...extra, 'origin', `HEAD:refs/heads/${branch}`]` (no `-u`); otherwise unchanged. The `--no-thin` retry keeps working for both. The verb passes `detached: current === 'HEAD'` (and the injected `deps.push` gets `(branch, { detached })`).

`usage()`: add `'        mc publish --branch <name>          a detached HEAD (a mend\'s worktree) to that branch\n'`. Help text and `docs/mc-command-matrix.md`: add `[--branch <b>]` to the usage and one clause, 'a detached HEAD only with `--branch`'.

Tests in `tests/mc/publish.test.js` (the fixture's `rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` answers `branch`; let `deps.push` record its second argument): (1) `'a detached HEAD publishes to --branch without -u'` — `branch: 'HEAD'`, `run(['--branch', 'step-x'])` returns 0, `pushed` is `['step-x']` with `{ detached: true }`, and `pushBranch` called with `detached: true` and a fake `spawn` receives `['push', 'origin', 'HEAD:refs/heads/step-x']`; (2) `'--branch on another branch, or an invalid name, refuses before the network'` — `branch: 'other'` with `['--branch', 'step-x']` returns 2 and no gh call; the fixture answers `check-ref-format` with `null` for `'bad..name'` and that returns 2; (3) `'a detached HEAD without --branch is still refused'` — `branch: 'HEAD'`, no flags, returns 1 with `on HEAD` in stderr.

steps.title: The retry preamble, the mend prompt, the hook and the toolbox send every push through `mc publish`
steps.done_when: Success criterion 2's grep finds nothing, `node --test --import ./tests/_isolate-home.mjs tests/mc/hooks.test.js tests/mc/mend.test.js tests/mc/run-plan.test.js` passes, and `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why (ruling 43): `retryPreamble` (`src/mc/run-plan.js`, ~line 800) says 'push to the same branch, and run `mc merge …` again', and `mendPrompt` (`src/mc/mend.js`, ~line 143) says `git push origin HEAD:${branch}` — which the pre-tool hook refuses. 21 of 125 sessions since 2026-09-26 pushed by hand and 8 landed a stale description.

`retryPreamble`: replace the two lines 'Start there — `gh pr view` and the diff — fix what the gate named (never by' / 'lowering a threshold or skipping a test), push to the same branch, and run' with 'Start there — `gh pr view` and the diff — fix what the gate named (never by' / 'lowering a threshold or skipping a test), commit, run `mc publish` (it pushes to the same branch and lists your commits under the description; `--body-file` when the description itself is now wrong), and run'. The next line (`mc merge … again. No new pull request.`) stays.

`mendPrompt`: replace '- Commit, then `git push origin HEAD:${branch}`. No force.' with '- Commit, then `mc publish --branch ${branch}` — it pushes without force and lists the commit under the pull request\'s description. Never `git push`.'

`src/mc/hooks.js` `BASH_RULES`: after `pr-create`, add `{ id: 'pr-edit', test: /(^|[;&|(]\s*|\s)gh\s+pr\s+edit\b/u, reason: 'Use `mc publish` — on an open pull request `--title`, `--body-file` and `--base` each edit only their own field, and without a body it lists the commits after the description.' }`. Change the `push` rule's reason to: 'Use `mc publish` — it pushes without force, refuses on main, a dirty tree or a moved remote, and opens or updates the PR; `--branch <name>` from a detached HEAD. A deliberate force-with-lease (a rebased stack) carries MC_HOOK_ALLOW=1.' `TOOLBOX`: the publish line becomes `'  publish           mc publish [--title … --body-file … --base …]   (push + open/update the PR, never force)'`.

`src/mc/help-text.js`, the `mc hook pre-tool` entry: 'gh pr create and git push → mc publish' becomes 'gh pr create, gh pr edit and git push → mc publish', keeping the wrapping of the entry's other lines. `docs/technical/mc-hooks.md` § `mc hook pre-tool`: name `gh pr edit` beside `gh pr create` wherever the rules are listed.

Tests: `tests/mc/mend.test.js` line ~187 expects `/mc publish --branch mq/u` instead of `/git push origin HEAD:mq/u`, and add `assert.doesNotMatch(prompt, /git push/u)`. In `tests/mc/hooks.test.js`, add to the rule tests: `gh pr edit 12 --body-file x` is refused with the `pr-edit` reason, `MC_HOOK_ALLOW=1 gh pr edit 12 --base main` passes, `echo gh pr edit` is not refused (follow how the `pr-create` cases are written). If a test in `tests/mc/run-plan.test.js` pins the retry preamble text, update it to the new text; add `assert.match(…, /mc publish/u)` there.

steps.title: `mc merge` refuses an unpushed head and a conflicting pull request before queueing
steps.done_when: `node --test --import ./tests/_isolate-home.mjs tests/mc/merge-command.test.js` passes with the new tests, and `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why (ruling 43): sessions ran `git push … | tail; mc merge …`, so a failed push queued a head nobody meant; and 30 rounds since 2026-09-26 stopped on a conflict with main only after waiting in the queue, when the session that could resolve it had ended. `mc publish` already prints `state dirty` without refusing.

In `queueForMerger` (`src/mc/commands/repo.js`, ~line 362): ask `gh pr view <pr> --json headRefName,headRefOid,mergeable` instead of `headRefName` alone, keeping `head` as today. Then, before `stepForMerge`: (a) when `mergeable === 'CONFLICTING'`, write `mc: #${pr} conflicts with its base on GitHub — merge origin/main into the branch here (git fetch -q origin && git merge origin/main), resolve, mc publish, then mc merge again\n` to stderr and return 1; `MERGEABLE` and `UNKNOWN` (GitHub is still computing) pass. (b) The caller's worktree is `deps.cwd || process.cwd()`; read its branch with `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` there (through `deps.git` when given, else `tryGit` from `../git.js`). Only when that branch equals `head`: read the worktree's `rev-parse HEAD` and `ls-remote --heads origin <head>` (first field); when they differ, write `mc: this worktree holds ${head} at ${local.slice(0, 7)}, origin at ${remote ? remote.slice(0, 7) : 'nothing'} — mc publish first, then mc merge\n` and return 1. A worktree on another branch, or outside git, is not checked. Nothing is queued and no round is recorded on either refusal.

Write the refusals as a small pure function in the same file, `doorRefusal({ pr, mergeable, head, worktreeBranch, localHead, remoteHead })` returning the message or null, and call it; the batch path (`opts.prs`) goes through `queueForMerger` and so gets the same refusals per pull request.

Tests in `tests/mc/merge-command.test.js`, following the fixtures there (inject `deps.gh`, `deps.git`, `deps.cwd`): (1) `'a pull request GitHub reports CONFLICTING is refused at the door and nothing is queued'`; (2) `'the branch checked out here at a head origin does not have is refused: mc publish first'`; (3) `'a worktree on another branch, and UNKNOWN mergeability, are queued as before'`. Existing fixtures whose `gh pr view` answers only `headRefName` must still queue (no `mergeable` is not `CONFLICTING`). Add one sentence to `docs/technical/mc-merge.md` where the door's refusals are described (find 'plan-trespass'): 'Before that, the door refuses a pull request GitHub reports CONFLICTING, and one whose branch the caller's worktree holds at a head origin does not have (ruling 43).'

steps.title: The merger lands only the head it measured: `--match-head-commit`
steps.done_when: `grep -n 'match-head-commit' src/mc/repo-merge.js` finds the landing call, `node --test --import ./tests/_isolate-home.mjs tests/mc/repo-merge.test.js tests/mc/merger.test.js` passes with the new tests, and `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why (ruling 43): `repo-merge.js` (~line 293) runs `gh pr merge <n> --squash` with no head pinned, so a push that lands during a round is squashed unmeasured; the tree check only notices after the merge.

`freshenBranchForLanding` (`src/mc/repo-freshen.js`): return the full sha as well — `{ ok: true, at, sha }` where `sha` is the untruncated `rev-parse HEAD` (keep `at` as the 7-character form for the existing message).

In the landing loop of `src/mc/repo-merge.js`: the expected head is the freshened `sha` when the branch was freshened, else the measured head — `verdict.pr.head_sha` for one pull request, the batch item's `head_sha` (`(verdict.prs || []).find((item) => item.number === number)?.head_sha`) in a batch. Before merging, read `gh pr view <n> --json headRefOid` up to 6 times, 5 s apart (through the injected sleep if the file has one; otherwise add a `sleep` dep defaulting to a `setTimeout` promise, so tests pass `async () => {}`), until it equals the expected head; GitHub lags a push by seconds (see the comment at `repo-gate.js` ~line 1146). If it never does, `finish('drift', `#${n} is at ${short(actual)} on GitHub, not the ${short(expected)} this round measured — not merged`)`. Then `gh pr merge <n> --squash --match-head-commit <expected>`. With no expected head known (null), merge as today and say so with `say`.

Tests in `tests/mc/repo-merge.test.js`, following its fakes: (1) `'the landing pins the measured head'` — the recorded `gh pr merge` call contains `--match-head-commit` and the measured sha; (2) `'a freshened branch is landed at the freshened head'` — with a `refresh` fake returning `{ ok: true, at: 'fffffff', sha: 'f'.repeat(40) }`, the pin is that sha; (3) `'a head GitHub never reports is drift, and nothing is merged'` — `headRefOid` stays another sha; no `pr merge` call, stop `drift`. Update any existing assertion that deep-equals the merge call to the new arguments. Add one sentence to `docs/technical/mc-merge.md` where the squash is described: 'The squash is pinned with `--match-head-commit` to the head the round measured or freshened, once GitHub reports it (ruling 43).'
